visual.general_description: Black-and-white flowchart of a proposed management pathway for irreducible groin hernia (strangulation screening, bedside reduction, emergency laparoscopy, resection, mesh vs tissue repair).
visual.detailed_description: Black-on-white flowchart of rectangular boxes joined by arrows with Yes/No labels. Top-left box (split by a dashed line): "Investigations BEFORE reduction" with bullets "Clinical exam" and "Labs: NLR, D-dimer, CPK (± lactate, LDH)"; below the dashed line "Signs of strangulation?" with bullets "Skin changes, fever, peritonism", "Symptoms >24 h" and "NLR >~6.5, D-dimer >300, CPK >140" (no units printed). A "No" arrow goes right to "Attempt bedside manual reduction with appropriate analgesia/sedation", then down to "Successful?"; "Yes" goes to "Observe (short stay) & plan early repair (same admission or soon)" and "No" returns by a long diagonal arrow to the "Emergency operation" box. A bold "Yes" arrow from the first box also goes down to "Emergency operation". The Emergency operation box (split by a dashed line) reads "Diagnostic laparoscopy ± gentle reduction" and "Adjunct: ICG perfusion assessment" and leads to "Bowel viable?"; "Yes" goes to "TAPP mesh repair in preperitoneal space"; "No" goes down to a bold box "Resection (intra- or extracorporeal); restore bowel continuity." with italic text "If intracorporeal is not feasible → consider the modified McEvedy high approach." From it two arrows lead to "Clean-contaminated → Mesh repair feasible" and "Gross contamination → Primary tissue repair (no mesh). Plan delayed elective mesh repair ≈ 6 weeks (TEP/TAPP or open anterior approach)."
